title: Computer Related Offences (Hacking / Data Tampering)
summary: Penalizes dishonest or fraudulent acts specified under section 43 including unauthorized data downloading, disruption, and system intrusion.
fullText: If any person, dishonestly or fraudulently, does any act which destroys, deletes or alters any information residing in a computer resource or diminishes its value or utility... he shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years or with fine which may extend to five lakh rupees or with both.
plainExplanation: Covers unauthorized account access, password cracking, malware injection, server tampering, or altering digital data without authorization.
punishment: Imprisonment up to 3 years or fine up to ₹5,00,000, or both.

title: Punishment for Identity Theft
summary: Penalizes fraudulent or dishonest use of electronic signature, password, or unique identification feature of any other person.
fullText: Whoever, fraudulently or dishonestly make use of the electronic signature, password or any other unique identification feature of any other person, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years and shall also be liable to fine which may extend to rupees one lakh.
plainExplanation: Applies when someone steals or fraudulently uses your passwords, OTPs, Aadhaar details, social media credentials, or biometrics.
punishment: Imprisonment up to 3 years and fine up to ₹1,00,000.

title: Punishment for Cheating by Personation by Using Computer Resource
summary: Penalizes cheating by personating another person through a computer resource or communication device.
fullText: Whoever, by means of any communication device or computer resource; cheats by personating, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years and shall also be liable to fine which may extend to one lakh rupees.
plainExplanation: Key statute for UPI scams, fake customer care numbers, QR code fraud, and impersonating banks or authority figures through digital devices.
punishment: Imprisonment up to 3 years and fine up to ₹1,00,000.

title: Punishment for Violation of Privacy
summary: Penalizes intentional capturing, publishing, or transmitting images of private area of any person without consent.
fullText: Whoever, intentionally or knowingly captures, publishes or transmits the image of a private area of any person without his or her consent, under circumstances violating the privacy of that person, shall be punished with imprisonment which may extend to three years or with fine not exceeding two lakh rupees, or with both.
plainExplanation: Addresses non-consensual sharing or threatening to share intimate photos or videos online, digital voyeurism, and sextortion threats.
punishment: Imprisonment up to 3 years or fine up to ₹2,00,000, or both.
